lesson.text: Rational numbers can be written as fractions: 3/4, −2, 0.5 and 0.333… (which is 1/3) are all rational. Their decimals end or repeat.
Irrational numbers can't be written as fractions. Their decimals go on forever without repeating: √2 = 1.41421…, π = 3.14159…
The square root of a number that isn't a square number is irrational: √2, √3, √5, √10.
Estimate by squaring: 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so √55 is between 7 and 8, a little closer to 7.

exercises.hint: Its decimal never ends or repeats.

exercises.prompt: √30 lies between which two whole numbers?
π can be written exactly as a fraction.
exercises.explain: No: 22/7 is only close; π is irrational.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best estimate of √50?
exercises.explain: 50 is just above 49, so a little over 7.

exercises.prompt: Put in order, smallest first: √10, 3, π
Between which whole number and the next is √90? Give the smaller one.
